answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make trust climb a slow spiral: a new identity starts with tiny, peer-reviewed jobs, and only a long public record of verified work lifts it toward high-value tasks, layer by layer like shale pressed into a ridge. Spinning up a hundred fake identities is cheap, but forging a hundred deep, cross-checked histories costs more than any reward the swarm could steal, so the attack stops paying for itself.
